name: Clank Bass
description: A modulator at 1.41 times the key strikes inharmonic overtones that die fast over a round body: a bass with a metallic clank.

name: Detuned Bass
description: Two pairs a few cents apart beating against each other, each a little bright: a thick, moving bass.

name: Fretless Bass
description: One key at a time, gliding where the notes touch, a soft modulator that swells a little after the strike: a singing fretless bass.

name: Fuzz Bass
description: A modulator moving itself at full feedback, driven hard and held: a buzzing, distorted bass.

name: Glide Bass
description: One key at a time with a quick glide, a saw-like modulator by its feedback: a sliding synth bass.

name: Half Wave Bass
description: A carrier playing the sine's first half alone, its second silent, under a modulator of the same wave: a nasal, digital bass.

name: Hollow Bass
description: A carrier under a modulator at twice the key, which gives odd harmonics only, like a square: a hollow, woody synth bass.

name: Log Bass
description: A carrier struck by a modulator at four times the key, both dying fast: a wooden, marimba-like bass.

name: Octave Bass
description: Two pairs an octave apart, the lower one rounder: a full bass that doubles itself.

name: Organ Bass
description: Sines at the key, an octave up and two octaves up, held and then let go: an organ's pedal bass.

name: Pick Bass
description: A carrier and a modulator at the key, the modulator bright at the pick and darkening as the string rings, with a click from a modulator three times the key: a picked electric bass.

name: Pluck Bass
description: A pair struck and gone within half a second, bright at first: a short plucked bass for busy lines.

name: Pulse Bass
description: A carrier under a modulator playing the sine squared, which gives odd harmonics and a hollow pulse: a reedy bass.

name: Punch Bass
description: A stack of two modulators, the top one decaying fast so the bass starts hard and settles: a tight, punchy synth bass.

name: Rubber Bass
description: One carrier at half the key's pitch under three modulators: one that holds a round body, one that snaps at the start and one more over it at three times the key that adds a click: a punchy, rubbery bass.

name: Rumble Bass
description: A sine played low with a soft modulator, a quieter sine an octave over it, and a slow wobble of the amplitude: a dark rumble under a track.

name: Saw Bass
description: A carrier under a modulator that moves itself by its feedback at full, a saw's buzz that the envelope closes a little after the strike: a synth bass with an edge.

name: Slap Bass
description: A carrier with its modulator snapping hard and falling within a beat, and a second carrier struck by a modulator seven times the key for the pop of a string slapped against the frets.

name: Snap Bass
description: Three modulators on one carrier, one snapping open and shut, one holding, one at three times the key for a click: a punchy, synth-like bass.

name: Solid Bass
description: A carrier under a modulator at the key that strikes bright and settles to a round body, and a sine an octave under it: a solid, all-purpose bass.

name: Sub Sine Bass
description: A sine with a breath of second harmonic from a faint modulator: a deep, clean sub.

name: Thumb Bass
description: A round pair with a burst of a fixed high frequency at the strike: a thumbed bass with a click.

name: Touch Bass
description: Modulators that answer the velocity hard, so a soft note is round and a hard one barks: a bass that follows the hands.

name: Upright Bass
description: A carrier lightly moved at the key, dying away as a plucked string does, faster up the keys, and a low thump at the start: an upright bass.

name: Wah Bass
description: A modulator whose envelope rises a moment after the key and falls back, so each note opens and closes: a bass through a wah.

name: Wire Bass
description: A carrier under a modulator at twice the key and a high one at five, all bright at the pick and falling to a steel ring: a bass with round-wound strings.

name: Bell Pad
description: A struck bell over a pad that swells in after it, the bell's modulator at 3.5 times the key: bells that turn into a choir.

name: Bowed Bell
description: A bell's modulator at 3.5 times the key swelling in slowly rather than struck: a bell played with a bow.

name: Bright Chime
description: Three carriers struck by modulators at the key times 3.5, ringing out quickly: a bright chime for arpeggios.

name: Church Bell
description: Modulators at 3.5 and 1.4 times the key over carriers a little apart, ringing for seconds: a large, deep bell.

name: Cow Bell
description: Fixed frequencies at 560 and 845 hertz, a modulator ringing between them, short: a cowbell.

name: Crystal Bell
description: Modulators at 5.19 and 7 times the key, high and glittering, a long ring: struck glass.

name: Glass Bell
description: Modulators at four and a half times the key over carriers a few cents apart, dying away over seconds, and a high pair that rings only at the strike: a clear, glassy bell.

name: Gong
description: Modulators at 1.41 and 2.83 times the key, the first swelling a moment, ringing for seconds: a gong.

name: Hand Bell
description: Modulators at twice and 4.24 times the key, a clean ring: a small hand bell.

name: Music Box
description: A sine an octave and a half up, struck by a modulator at seven times the key and ringing briefly: a music box's comb.

name: Tubular Bell
description: A modulator at 3.5 times the key, bright at the strike and ringing on: an orchestra's tubular bells.

name: Brass Section
description: Four carriers a few cents apart, one an octave up, two of them moved by the feedback's operator for a saw's edge, each opening a little slowly from a pitch a touch flat, and a vibrato that comes in late: a brass section.

name: Brass Stabs
description: Horns whose carriers fall away within a beat, the modulator snapping: short brass stabs.

name: Brass Swell
description: Horns that crescendo over half a second, the modulator opening last: brass swelling into each chord.

name: Bright Brass
description: Four carriers under a saw-like modulator that opens hard: a bright brass section that cuts.

name: Fanfare
description: The section with a fifth carrier a fifth up, bright and quick: open chords for fanfares.

name: French Horns
description: A darker section, the octave carrier quiet and the modulator moderate, a slow swell and late vibrato: French horns.

name: Low Brass
description: The section an octave lower in its carriers and darker: trombones and tubas.

name: Soft Brass
description: The section with its modulator low and slow to open: mellow horns for held chords.

name: Synth Brass
description: Two saw-like pairs detuned wide, swelling: a synthesizer's brass rather than a section's.

name: Trumpet Section
description: The section with a quick fall in pitch into each note and a bright modulator: a trumpet section's attack.

name: Alarm
description: Two pitches a fourth apart on the LFO's square, a bright tone: an alarm.

name: Clock Tick
description: A short, high, inharmonic strike: a clock's tick, for a rhythm part.

name: Laser Drop
description: One carrier moved by an operator that moves itself by its feedback at full, a saw's buzz; the pitch envelope starts four octaves up at each key and falls to it: a laser's drop.

name: Metal Hit
description: Modulators at 1.41 and 3.17 times the key, hard and ringing a second: a struck sheet of metal.

name: Noise Wash
description: A carrier moved by an operator at full feedback and a fixed high frequency, turning to noise, swelling slowly: wind or surf.

name: Riser
description: A saw-like tone whose pitch climbs two octaves on the pitch envelope while its modulator opens: a build-up.

name: Sci-Fi Computer
description: The LFO's sample and hold throwing the pitch about each step: a computer chattering.

name: Synth Tom
description: A sine whose pitch falls from a fifth over the key as it dies, a click of noise at the strike: an electronic tom.

name: Thunder Rumble
description: A low carrier under an operator at full feedback, fixed low and loud, dying over seconds: distant thunder.

name: Water Drop
description: A sine whose pitch jumps up and falls at once, a soft modulator with it: drops of water.

name: Bark Piano
description: The body's modulators answering the velocity hard, so a firm key growls: an electric piano that barks.

name: Bright Tine Piano
description: The tine modulator at fourteen times the key loud at the strike, ringing like a bell over the body: a bright electric piano.

name: Celesta
description: A sine struck by a modulator at seven times the key that dies at once, ringing on softly: a celesta's struck plates.

name: Electric Grand
description: Two piano pairs a little apart with a modulator at the key's 1.01 for the beating of a short-stringed grand, bright at the hammer: an electric grand piano.

name: Funk Clav
description: Three carriers at the key, an octave up and the key again, under modulators at three, five and the key with its feedback, all short and bright with the velocity: a funky clav.

name: Glass Piano
description: Pairs at the key with modulators at three and five times it, both decaying: a glassy, digital piano.

name: Grand Keys
description: Three carriers a little apart under modulators that are bright at the hammer and darken as the note dies, faster up the keys: an FM grand piano.

name: Harpsichord
description: Carriers at the key and an octave up, each under a hard modulator that fades a little, the notes ringing on: a plucked, bright harpsichord.

name: Honky Keys
description: Two piano pairs tuned a little apart so they beat: an out-of-tune upright.

name: Muted Clav
description: A pair with a modulator at three times the key, all short, the strings damped: a muted clav.

name: Punchy Tine Piano
description: An electric piano whose body holds up and whose strike is short and hard: a compressed, punchy piano for pop chords.

name: Reed Piano
description: A carrier on the half wave under a modulator moving itself a little, its body dying away: a reedy electric piano.

name: Soft Tine Piano
description: Three pairs with their modulators low, the tine faint: a mellow electric piano for ballads.

name: Tine Piano
description: Three pairs of a carrier and a modulator a little apart in pitch; the first pair's modulator at fourteen times the key gives the tine's bright strike, and the others the bark that a harder key brings: an electric piano.

name: Toy Piano
description: A carrier with an inharmonic modulator at 4.2 times the key, short and bright: a toy piano's tines.

name: Tremolo Piano
description: A soft electric piano whose carriers the LFO's triangle swells and fades: a piano through a tremolo.

name: Bassoon Lead
description: A carrier under modulators at the key and twice it, played low, a buzzing double reed: a bassoon.

name: Bell Lead
description: A held carrier and a struck one at the key with an inharmonic modulator ringing at the strike: a lead with a bell in its attack.

name: Clarinet Lead
description: A modulator at twice the key for the clarinet's odd harmonics, swelling in with the breath: a woody reed.

name: Digital Lead
description: A carrier on the double-speed wave under a modulator on the half wave: a hard, digital lead with a nasal edge.

name: Ethnic Reed
description: A modulator at three times the key and another at five, both bright, a quick, wide vibrato: a nasal, folk reed.

name: Fifth Lead
description: Two pairs a fifth apart, a saw's buzz on the lower: a lead that plays in fifths.

name: Flute Lead
description: A sine with a faint second harmonic, a soft swell and a breath of noise from a fixed high modulator at the start, a slow vibrato: a flute.

name: Glass Lead
description: A pair with its modulator at three times the key, bright and steady, and a second pair a little sharp: a glassy, chiming lead.

name: Gliding Lead
description: One carrier under three modulators, the last with its feedback at full for a saw's edge, played one key at a time and gliding between them, a vibrato that comes in late: a singing lead.

name: Growl Lead
description: A carrier under a modulator a semitone flat of the key, beating hard against it, and a saw's buzz: a growling, rough lead.

name: Mono Glide Lead
description: One key at a time with a long glide, two modulators on one carrier, bright and held: a lead that slides.

name: Oboe Lead
description: A carrier at the key moved by a modulator at the key and another at three times it, the upper partials strong: a nasal, double-reed lead.

name: Organ Lead
description: Sines at the key, two and three times it, and a short click at four: an organ lead with a percussive strike.

name: Reed Lead
description: A carrier under a modulator moving itself a little, with a quick vibrato and a breathy start: a lead like a harmonica.

name: Saw Lead
description: A carrier under a modulator moving itself at full feedback, a saw's buzz, held bright with a late vibrato: the plain synth lead.

name: Sax Lead
description: A carrier under a modulator at the key and another at three times it, both opening with the breath and answering the velocity, a breath of noise and a late vibrato: a saxophone.

name: Soft Sine Lead
description: Two sines an octave apart with a faint modulator, a gentle swell and vibrato: a soft, round lead.

name: Square Lead
description: A modulator at twice the key, odd harmonics only, a little vibrato: a hollow, square-wave lead.

name: Sync Lead
description: A modulator whose envelope falls from hard to soft over a second at each note, sweeping its partials down as a synced oscillator does: a tearing lead.

name: Synth Brass Lead
description: A modulator that swells in after the carrier, a saw by its feedback, as a horn's tone opens: a brassy lead.

name: Trill Lead
description: The LFO's square moving the pitch a step up and back at each held note, a saw-like tone: a trilling lead.

name: Trumpet Lead
description: A saw-like modulator opening a moment after the carrier, a quick fall into the note: a solo trumpet.

name: Wah Lead
description: A modulator that rises and falls at each note, opening the sound like a mouth: a lead that says wah.

name: Whistle Lead
description: A sine an octave up alone, gliding from note to note with a quick vibrato: a whistled line.

name: Glockenspiel
description: Sines at two and 5.4 times the key, struck and ringing: a glockenspiel's steel bars.

name: Kalimba
description: A sine struck by a modulator at the key's 6.1, its overtone gone at once, the tone fading fast: a thumb piano.

name: Log Drum
description: A sine struck by a modulator at 1.5 times the key, with a short fall of pitch: a hollow log drum.

name: Soft Mallets
description: Sines at the key and four times it, struck softly and dying away: felt mallets on wooden bars.

name: Steel Drum
description: A carrier at the key and one an octave up, struck by modulators at 1.5 and 2.5 times it, a little pitch drop at the strike: a bright steel drum.

name: Steel Pan
description: Carriers at the key, an octave up and two octaves up, struck by modulators at one and a half and three times the key that die away faster than they do: a steel pan.

name: Vibraphone
description: A sine with a modulator at four times the key at the strike, ringing on with the LFO swelling its level: a vibraphone with its motor on.

name: Wood Block
description: A carrier at the key with a modulator at 2.5 times it, gone in a tenth of a second: hollow wood struck.

name: Wood Marimba
description: A carrier struck by a modulator at four times the key, and a second carrier at four times the key, each dying away fast, faster up the keys: a wooden marimba.

name: Xylophone
description: A carrier and a high one at three times the key struck by modulators that die at once, short and hard: a xylophone.

name: Accordion
description: Two reed pairs, each a modulator at the key with feedback over a carrier, tuned apart so they beat: an accordion's musette.

name: Combo Organ
description: Carriers on the squared sine and the half wave, an octave apart, with a quick vibrato: a thin, reedy combo organ.

name: Drawbar Organ
description: Six sines, every operator a carrier, at half, one, two, three, four and eight times the key, like an organ's drawbars, held while the key is down, the highest with a little feedback for bite: an organ.

name: Full Organ
description: Six sines from half the key to eight times it, all out, one with a little feedback: an organ with every drawbar pulled.

name: Gospel Organ
description: Sines at the key, two, three and four times it with a hard click, and a fast, wide vibrato: a gospel organ through its rotating speaker.

name: Jazz Organ
description: Sines at the key, at three times it, and an octave up, with a short percussive click at three: a jazz organ with its percussion on.

name: Pipe Organ
description: Sines at the key, an octave and a twelfth up, slow to speak and slow to die, with a reed's buzz from one modulated pair: a pipe organ.

name: Soft Organ
description: Sines at the key and an octave up, no click, a gentle swell: a soft flute organ for chords.

name: Breath Pad
description: A soft pad and a breath of noise from a fixed high modulator moving a high carrier: a pad with air in it.

name: Choir Pad
description: Carriers at the key and twice it with modulators at four and five times it, soft, swelling slowly with a vibrato: a choir's ah.

name: Dark Pad
description: Two pairs a little apart with their modulators low, slow and dark: a warm bed under a track.

name: Digital Pad
description: Carriers on the squared and the double-speed waves, a little apart: a hard-edged digital pad.

name: Glass Pad
description: Pairs with modulators at three times the key, slow in and out: a bright, glassy pad.

name: Organ Pad
description: Sines at the key, an octave and a twelfth up, slow in and out with a slow vibrato: a pad of drawbars.

name: Shimmer Pad
description: A soft pad with a high pair two octaves up whose level the LFO moves: a pad that shimmers.

name: Space Pad
description: Pairs with modulators at 1.41 times the key, faint and slow, the pitch drifting on a slow triangle: an uneasy, open pad.

name: Sweep Pad
description: A saw-like modulator whose level rises over two seconds and falls back: a pad that opens through its chord.

name: Voices Pad
description: Carriers at two, three and four times the key over a fundamental, their levels shaped like a vowel, slow with vibrato: voices singing oo.

name: Warm Pad
description: Three pairs, the carriers spread a few cents either side of the key and one an octave up, all rising slowly and holding, a slow vibrato under them: a warm pad.

name: Acoustic Guitar
description: Carriers at the key and an octave up struck by modulators at the key and three times it, the brightness fading first: a steel-string guitar.

name: Banjo Pluck
description: A bright carrier under a modulator at three times the key, both short, with a twang from feedback: a banjo.

name: Dulcimer
description: Two carriers a few cents apart struck by modulators at the key and at three, a long, beating ring: a hammered dulcimer.

name: Glass Pluck
description: A carrier under a modulator at seven times the key, ringing briefly: a glassy, digital pluck.

name: Harp
description: A sine and an octave over it with a soft modulator at the pluck, ringing a long while: a concert harp.

name: Koto
description: A carrier under a modulator moving itself a little, its tone falling from hard to soft, and a slight bend into the note: a koto.

name: Mute Guitar
description: A pair struck and damped in a tenth of a second, a click of a modulator at five: a palm-muted guitar.

name: Nylon Pluck
description: Two carriers, the key and a few cents over it, each struck by a modulator that dies away fast, the second's at four times the key, with no sustain: a plucked nylon string.

name: Pizzicato Strings
description: Two pairs a little apart, plucked and gone within half a second: strings plucked rather than bowed.

name: Sitar Pluck
description: A carrier under a modulator whose level rises after the pluck and falls, a buzzing bridge, with a high pair ringing in sympathy: a sitar.

name: Synth Pluck
description: A saw by its feedback that the envelope closes in a moment: a synth pluck, as a filter snapped shut.

name: Bright Strings
description: The section quick to speak and brighter, for runs and stabs.

name: Cello Section
description: The section an octave down and warmer: the cellos.

name: Slow Strings
description: Darker modulators and a long bow in and out: strings for slow passages.

name: Solo Violin
description: One carrier under a modulator at the key and another at three times it, a quick bow and a wide vibrato: a solo violin.

name: String Section
description: Three pairs a little apart, each a soft saw by a modulator at the key, bowing in and out slowly with a vibrato: a string section.

name: Tremolo Strings
description: The section with its level shaking fast on the LFO: strings bowed in tremolo.
